summary: Core, built CLI, and MCP tests prove that Fast starts at implementation with generated AC-1, combined test/review gates, and direct --test/--review completion shortcuts.
Core, built CLI, and MCP tests prove project.complex, empirical complex, and empirical_complex enter Specify and retain Design, Plan, Implement, Verify, and Review gates.
Core and MCP tests prove loop is a read-only idle, active, or terminal snapshot, while runtime and built-CLI checks reject request arguments.

Integration tests prove ordinary coding requests trigger managed skills and guidance that choose Fast only for tiny low-risk non-UI work, choose Complex otherwise, and continue returned packets to a terminal state.
Repository scans and distribution smoke tests prove normal help, docs, and generated guidance require no profile or JSON flags; programmatic output and low-level start remain available.
Compatibility tests resume existing Quick state and normalize legacy Strong state to Complex, while runtime guards, help, docs, skills, and MCP expose only Fast and Complex for new work.
